blocks.html: Cost Per Acquisition (CPA) is a marketing metric that measures the total cost required to acquire one paying customer.

CPA is a critical metric for evaluating the efficiency and profitability of marketing and sales efforts. It helps businesses understand how much they are spending to convert a prospect into a customer and whether those costs align with revenue goals and customer lifetime value.
CPA is calculated using the following formula:

items.html: (Total Marketing and Sales Expenses ÷ Number of New Customers Acquired)

blocks.html: Helps control and optimize customer acquisition costs
Identifies the most efficient marketing channels
Supports budget allocation and campaign planning
Aligns acquisition costs with customer lifetime value (CLV)
By tracking CPA, businesses can assess which channels and strategies deliver the most cost-effective results.
If a company spends ₹1,00,000 on marketing and sales in a month and acquires 100 new customers, its CPA is ₹1,000 per customer.
Cost Per Acquisition is a key indicator of how efficiently a business is converting investment into customers. Lowering CPA while maintaining quality leads is essential for sustainable growth.
